name: Ryan Pitylak
current_role: Executive Vice President of Growth, NinjaTrader (since May 2024); co-founder of ZenBusiness
profile: Austin-based marketer and entrepreneur (b. 1982) who co-founded ZenBusiness in 2015, a public-benefit corporation helping micro-businesses form and run companies, and served as its CMO; ZenBusiness reached a ~$1.7B valuation. In May 2024 he joined futures-trading platform NinjaTrader as EVP of Growth.
interesting_fact: Before ZenBusiness he co-founded and ran Unique Influence, a digital marketing firm acquired in 2015 by MDC Partners' media agency network Assembly.
deep_cut_fact: He earned undergraduate degrees in both economics and philosophy at the University of Texas.

public_contacts.value: https://ninjatrader.com/contact-us/ (has a Media & Communication Inquiries section)

notes: Wikipedia notes a 2004-06 spam-email history settled with Texas and Microsoft; avoid that topic. Now at NinjaTrader, so the ZenBusiness angle is past tense.

name: Yoni Tserruya
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Lusha (Tel Aviv / New York)
profile: Israeli software engineer who co-founded Lusha with Assaf Eisenstein in 2016; the B2B contact-data and sales-intelligence platform grew largely bootstrapped before a $205M Series B in 2021 at a $1.5B valuation. He still leads it as CEO, now pitching Lusha as a GTM data layer for AI agents via API and MCP.
interesting_fact: Lusha reached unicorn status in 2021 with a $205M Series B led by PSG at a $1.5B valuation after years of near-bootstrapped growth.
deep_cut_fact: Lusha began as a side project he built while working his first job as an iOS developer at AT&T, after studying computer science; he calls himself 'a builder at heart' who was 'more into tinkering than following plans'.
notes: Recent interview talks about AI agents and data infrastructure (MCP), a natural data/AI podcast angle.

name: Jiun Ee Teoh
current_role: Co-founder, CARSOME; CEO of CARSOME Academy
profile: Malaysian entrepreneur (known as 'JT') who co-founded CARSOME with Eric Cheng in 2015; it became Southeast Asia's largest integrated used-car e-commerce platform and Malaysia's first tech unicorn. A former COO and Chief Business Development Officer, he now runs CARSOME Academy, its accredited automotive training institution across Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.
interesting_fact: CARSOME started in 2015 as an advertising platform and pivoted through trial and error to a used-car marketplace; the founders now preach that 'growth at all costs isn't a good mindset' after steering it to profitability.
deep_cut_fact: As CEO of CARSOME Academy he has spearheaded training partnerships with Sunway University, UniMAP, Beijing Business School, IUKL and Malaysia's MCMC; the academy has trained 1,500+ students and 6,500 corporate employees as automotive technicians.
notes: Eric Cheng is the public face of CARSOME; Teoh's background before CARSOME was in digital media.

name: Shay Filosof
current_role: Co-founder and Senior Software Engineer, Orca Security (Tel Aviv)
profile: Israeli engineer and one of the eight co-founders of Orca Security (founded 2019), the agentless cloud-security company valued at $1.8B in 2021. Like several Orca founders he came from Check Point, where he was a software architect and R&D group manager; he remains at Orca in a hands-on engineering role building cloud-security products.
interesting_fact: Orca was founded by a group of eight ex-Check Point engineers and executives, an unusually large founding team, and pioneered 'SideScanning' agentless cloud security.
deep_cut_fact: At Check Point he worked on firewall gateway performance as a software architect and R&D group manager; he holds a BSc in CS from the Academic College of Tel Aviv-Yaffo and an MSc in CS from the Open University of Israel.
notes: Very low public profile; details come mainly from directory profiles (TheOrg, Crunchbase). CEO Avi Shua / Gil Geron are Orca's public faces; approach via Orca's comms.

name: Zhaopeng Chen
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Agile Robots SE (Munich)
profile: Chinese-born roboticist who completed his doctorate at the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and was deputy director of its Modular Dexterous Robotics Lab before co-founding Agile Robots with DLR scientist Peter Meusel in 2018. The Munich company makes force-sensitive AI-driven robot arms and systems and now the Agile ONE humanoid; it became a unicorn in 2021.
interesting_fact: At DLR he worked on the team that developed a widely acclaimed humanoid robotic hand, which became the basis of his first spin-off with Peter Meusel, Wessling Robotics, before Agile Robots.
deep_cut_fact: A lifelong science-fiction fan, he says getting into his Chinese university's robotics institute 'was not easy'; from his third year he built robot hands and arms end-to-end, and at DLR spent years on robotic systems for outer space.
notes: No published press email found (site is JS-heavy); use the company website or DLR spin-off page (https://www.dlr.de/en/rm/transfer/spin-offs/agile-robots) for context. Space-robotics and humanoid angle fits a deep-tech podcast.

name: Mahesh Vellanki
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Partner, SuperLayer (Web3 venture studio); co-founder of Forte and Rally (RLY) (current status unverified)
profile: Former Redpoint Ventures investor (Principal, 2012-18; earlier Citi investment banking) who co-founded blockchain-gaming platform Forte with Kevin Chou and others, which reached a $1B+ valuation in 2021. With Chou he also co-founded the Rally/RLY social-token network and in 2021 the crypto venture studio SuperLayer.
interesting_fact: SuperLayer launched in Oct 2021 with backing from Marc Andreessen, Chris Dixon and Michael Ovitz, and in 2022 Polygon led a $25M fund for the studio.
deep_cut_fact: He moved from VC to founder: after six years as a Principal at Redpoint Ventures, he partnered with Kabam founder Kevin Chou; he studied finance at the University of Maryland's Robert H. Smith School of Business.
notes: No published contact found; low public profile since 2022. Rally/RLY wound down; confirm current focus before outreach. Education detail from directory profiles (MarketScreener/TheOrg).

name: Austin Allison
profile: Cincinnati-raised entrepreneur who founded real-estate transaction software dotloop in 2009, sold it to Zillow in 2015 (reported ~$108-120M) and ran it inside Zillow until 2018. He then co-founded Pacaso (2020), which sells co-owned second homes via property-specific LLCs; it hit a $1B valuation within five months, then a record for a US startup.
interesting_fact: Pacaso reached unicorn status in about five months after launch in 2020, among the fastest ever for a US startup.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in a small town north of Cincinnati, the son of a carpenter, and says he was 'swinging a hammer starting at age three or four'; watching his father show up every day to provide shaped his work ethic.
notes: Frequent podcast guest and speaker; receptive to founder-story interviews.
